thread:
maria: quick update — ran a small bringup for the 40b-quant (q4f16) across h100-80 / a100-40 in us-east1 and eu-west1. p99 on a100 is higher than expected, need to figure kernel choices + autoscale headroom for dedicated clusters
aj: bench summary (all single-model pools, seq=1024, batch=auto):
```
us-east1 h100-80: p50 85ms, p95 210ms, p99 420ms, thpt 610 tok/s
us-east1 a100-40: p50 120ms, p95 320ms, p99 760ms, thpt 380 tok/s
eu-west1 h100-80: p50 95ms, p95 230ms, p99 480ms, thpt 580 tok/s
eu-west1 a100-40: p50 130ms, p95 350ms, p99 820ms, thpt 360 tok/s
```
notes: h100 kernels (fused-attn-v2 + quant-opt) are ~1.6x faster on p99 vs a100 with current nv-fused path. a100 seems more sensitive to batching patterns and tail effects.
kenji: looks like we hit kv-cache warmup + slab packing differences. a100 p99 spikes when concurrent short requests interleave long ones. two quick ideas: 1) prefer continous-batching mode with per-slot affinity, 2) split pools by expected seq-length to avoid cross-request cache churn.
eva: for dedicated sizing we need concrete concurrency targets per GPU. what concurrency did you use for those benches?
aj: concurrency target during the run was 12 slots per GPU (single replica), effective concurrency ~9 due to batching collapse. throughput numbers are per-GPU with that concurrency.
samir: rule-of-thumb I use: plan for steady_concurrency = target_qps * avg_tokens / (gpu_tok_s) and then add headroom 25-35% for microbursts + warmup. For 40b-q on a100-40, gpu_tok_s ~= 360 tok/s (from bench), avg_tokens ~120 => concurrency_per_gpu ~= (qps*120)/360.
maria: example calc: if product needs 50 r/s (requests/sec) * 120 tokens = 6000 tok/s => need 6000/360 ~= 17 concurrent slots on a100 -> with 12 slots/GPU typical, that's ~2 GPUs. but p99 tail means we should add headroom and warmup: recommend 30% headroom + 2 warmup slots per GPU. so size to 3 GPUs in dedicated pool.
kenji: on a100 specifically, kernel fallback costs matter. We saw a ~40-60ms penalty when falling back from fused-attn to generic kernels on long tails. Can we ensure scheduler prefers h100 for latency-sensitive routes and a100 for batch/non-critical?
eva: that implies routing policy + SLA tiers. For Dedicated we can expose route->pool mapping in rollout config. Also need autoscale params: what min/max and cooldown?
ops-bot: canary created: dedicated/40b-quant-canary - min_replicas=1, max_replicas=6, cooldown=120s.
samir: suggest autoscale config for prod pools: min=2, max=12, step=2, cooldown=180s, warmup_slots=2. Reason: the warmup_slots prevent sudden cold-start p99s when scale up happens.
aj: small perf note — prefix caching (per-customer) reduced median by ~10% and p95 by ~12% in h100 runs. on a100 it helped median but didn't fully remove the p99 spikes.
maria: action items: @kenji evaluate per-pool kernel policy (fused-attn-v2 preferred) + fallback thresholds; @eva add route->pool SLA mapping to the dedicated config; @aj run an interleaved short/long request bench to reproduce a100 tail and attach raw logs; @samir propose autoscale default config for new 40b pools.
eva: I'll draft the config PR with routing and autoscale defaults, will include canary.
kenji: I'll test per-slot affinity and continuous-batching affinity to see if it flattens p99 on a100. quick test plan: 1) run 30m interleaved short/long workload 2) enable affinity 3) measure p99 delta.
maria: thanks team. let's reconvene after the tests — aim to lock dedicated pool sizing and autoscale defaults by EOD Friday. :thumbsup:
